1. A stronger all-$g$ return theorem

Consider the unital baseline on an isolated region of $m\ge1$ qubits. Normalize $\gamma=1$, and write
$\mathcal L_0=-i[H,\cdot]+\sum_{i=1}^{m}(E_i-\mathrm{Id}),
\qquad
\Phi_t=e^{t\mathcal L_0},
\qquad
\mathcal E(X)=\operatorname{Tr}(X)\frac{I}{2^m}.$
For this lemma, $H$ can be any finite Hermitian matrix. Neither its norm nor its locality enters the bound.

For $0<\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mix}}\le1$, define
$p=\max\{2,m\},\qquad
s=\frac12\log(p-1),\qquad
u=\log\frac{24m}{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mix}}},
\qquad
t_*=2s+u.$
Then
$\boxed{
(1-\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mix}})\mathcal E
\ \le_{\mathrm{cp}}\ 
\Phi_t
\ \le_{\mathrm{cp}}\ 
(1+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mix}})\mathcal E,
\qquad t\ge t_* .
}
\tag{1}$
Here $\Psi\le_{\mathrm{cp}}\Phi$ means that $\Phi-\Psi$ is completely positive. This is stronger than an additive trace-distance or diamond-distance estimate.


What the relative bound guarantees

For every untouched reference $R$, of arbitrary dimension, and every joint input state $\omega_{SR}$,
$\boxed{
(1-\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mix}})
\left(\frac{I_S}{2^m}\otimes\omega_R\right)
\le
(\Phi_t\otimes\mathrm{Id}_R)(\omega_{SR})
\le
(1+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mix}})
\left(\frac{I_S}{2^m}\otimes\omega_R\right).
}
\tag{2}$
No independence assumption is imposed on $\omega_{SR}$. Because this is operator order, conditioning on an arbitrarily rare measurement event on the untouched reference preserves the corresponding relative estimate.

Equation (1) also gives an exact positive decomposition
$\Phi_t=(1-\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mix}})\mathcal E
+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mix}}\Psi,$
where $\Psi$ is unital CPTP and
$0\le_{\mathrm{cp}}\Psi\le_{\mathrm{cp}}2\mathcal E.
\tag{3}$
This is a mathematical representation of the allowed channel. It does not introduce a free physical reset, an observed environmental flag, or a new control interface.

Restoring units, the physical time is $t_*/\gamma$. A rational upper bound for the normalized time is
$\left\lceil\log_2\bigl(\max\{2,m\}-1\bigr)\right\rceil
+
\left\lceil\log_2\frac{24m}{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mix}}}\right\rceil
+2.
\tag{4}$
The ceilings are computable by integer comparisons on the rational input.


Proof: a nuclear-norm estimate between two smoothing intervals

The proof avoids a complete-hypercontractivity assumption.
